Closer to Gothic than TES, despite the comparisons that mostly seem to focus on the fact the game is primarily a FPP RPG. 

Good exploration, world design and writing. Serviceable (if not very ambitious) combat. Good zero to hero character progression that makes you feel very powerful in the mid to late game. Hub based rather than a true open worlder (which is no bad thing, the hubs are pretty huge).

Loses some marks for polish issues in the late game (last chapter feels quite rushed), also fairly inconsistent performance (thanks Unity).

Overall a very solid RPG that should appeal to fans of the Gothic series. With a few patches it will be a superb game, though even with some polish and performance issues is still a very good game as of this review.

Humongous Entertainment was way before their time. Pajama Sam is a hilarious, interesting kid's game with changing routes, so that you can play multiple times with different challenges and goals. There are always things to click on, more funny dialouge to hear, and dozens and dozens of socks to look for. I loved Pajama Sam as a child and still do now, and honestly, find it even funnier now than I ever did as a child. 

As an adult, it took me 1 hour to finish the game, with prior experience. There is no save feature that I could find, so keep that in mind. On Windows 10, the game plays much better on windowed mode, so press Alt + enter for the game to run better. :) Enjoy!

This game doesn't really have any lows but it also doesn't have any highs: it's just a straight mediocrity from start to finish. I'd say the twist is not bad but it definitely needed better writers to sell the horror associated with it.

And get a load of this: the game has so many cutscenes (not a bad thing by itself), it also has a flowchart because you are expected to try different scenarios... but it doesn't have a way to skip cutscenes! Supermassive Games has been making this type of game for at least since Until Dawn in 2015! Are you freaking telling me they somehow have not invented this technology yet?!

This game is honestly just too deep for me. It feels tailor-made for the type of MMORPG player who loves "doing nothing", those who enjoy getting lost in endless side systems and life-sim fluff rather than a focused narrative.

The combat attempts a Souls-like vibe with its parries and dodges. The real challenge isn't the bosses, it's the mobile-game-style "power level" walls. You’ll be progressing fine until you hit a hard ceiling that demands a grind to upgrade your stats before you can move on.

It’s essentially a much prettier, PC-version of KingsRoad. It offers way more to do and hides its gacha mechanics a bit better, but the DNA is the same. If you want a world to live in and don't mind a grindy loop, you'll love it. For me, it's just a bit too much noise.
